chapter_title: Concerning the Three Blows that befell the Enemy because of the Light.
chapter_note: Nearly the whole chapter is impersonal, system-description eschatology: three sequential ‘blows’/wars and the final binding/separation of Darkness. Only the opening dialogue-attribution (‘Once again he turned, and says:’) is a later compilation frame; no NT citation and no institutional/pastoral application occurs.

paragraphs.core_text: The Darkness itself, the Enemy, has received three bad blows with three wars; and worse dangers from the Light in those three wars.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution: “Once again he turned, and says:” (hagiographic/compilation frame marker).
paragraphs.temporal_note: The opening speech-attribution is a Kephalaia framing device, but the sentence that follows is a schematic, numbered cosmological setup (‘three blows/three wars’) characteristic of the older teaching voice.

paragraphs.core_text: The first: (The Enemy) was brought out to the middle and separated from his dark earth, whence he had departed. He was vanquished in that first war, caught and [bound] by the Living Soul.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal cosmological mechanics (spatial separation, binding, named cosmic agent Living Soul) with no address to an audience and no reference to contemporary institutions.

paragraphs.core_text: The second blow is the time when he will be dissolved and melted, and he perishes in this great fire. He is destroyed and overthrown, from the images that are all by which he exists. And he will be gathered in [to the] fetter corresponding to his archetype, and be made like he was from the first beginning.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic eschatological process-description (dissolution, great fire, return-to-archetype) stays wholly within the cosmic system; no citation or exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: The third blow that will befall the Enemy is the 'rolling back' [at the] end when everything will be separated, and male will be divided [from] female. Now, the male will be bound in the lump, but the female [will be thrown] in to the tomb. For it will be divided [ ... by a great] stone in their midst, for generation upon generation, for ever and ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Eschatological separation schema (rolling back; male/female division; lump/tomb; stone barrier) functions as cosmological architecture, not moral instruction; the ‘for ever and ever’ closure is compatible with core apocalyptic diction.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.106⟩ This is the way that the binding of the Enemy will come about, in a fetter that is burdensome and strong, one from which there is never escape; because [they have achieved] his binding and bound him for ever. And they have achieved his being set apart, and he has been set apart for ever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues the same impersonal system-account of final binding (‘fetter… never escape’) without shifting into audience address or church discipline; no seam into institutional application despite chapter-level redaction concerns.
